subject: Civil Engineering
title: Rigid Pavements: Concrete Roads
description: Learn Rigid Pavements: Concrete Roads in one minute.

hook.text: An interstate through the Midwest uses concrete slabs — bumpy joints every 15 feet.

buildup.text: Rigid pavements use thick concrete slabs. The slab itself spreads the load over a wide area.

discovery.text: Joints prevent random cracking — saw-cut lines tell the concrete where to crack neatly.

twist.text: Dowel bars cross the joints — they transfer load between slabs while allowing expansion.

climax.text: Continuously reinforced concrete has no joints — steel holds the cracks tight.

punchline.text: Concrete roads last longer but cost more. The trade-off defines every project.

quiz.question: Why are joints cut into concrete pavement slabs?
options: To make the road more flexible under heavy traffic
To control where cracks form so they occur in neat, planned lines
To allow water to drain through the pavement surface
